Description: The human operator. They are an untrusted source of input; all actions from the user must be validated by the UI and App Logic.
The outer boundary representing the physical device's operating system (e.g., iOS/Android). It separates the device internals from the external world.
The isolated execution environment for your specific app. Code running here is "trusted" by your developers, but restricted by the OS.
The visual layer receiving touch/text input. It acts as the first line of defense, sanitizing user input before passing it to the Application Logic.
The "brain" of the app. It processes business rules and coordinates data flow. It is the most critical component to protect from injection attacks or logic flaws.
Private files (e.g., SQLite, Plist) accessible only by this app. Data here is relatively safe unless the device is rooted/jailbroken.
OS-level security features like FaceID, TouchID, or PIN. The app relies on the OS to verify the user without handling the actual biometric data.
Linked attributes:
Local Authentication Service
JWT
Authentication Token
Token-based authentication

Description: Hardware-backed secure storage (iOS Keychain / Android Keystore). This is where high-value secrets (session tokens, encryption keys) must be stored.
Public file space (e.g., SD Card, Photos folder). High Risk: Any app with permissions can read/write here; never store sensitive medical data (PHI) here.
The OS networking stack. It handles the TLS encryption tunnel. It is the gateway for data leaving the safe "Sandbox" to the hostile "Internet."
The native OS agent (e.g., Play Store app) that manages updates and integrity checks for the application binary.
Third-party Identity Provider (e.g., Google, Okta). The app delegates authentication here to avoid handling passwords directly.
The backend API servers. This is the ultimate destination for data. The app must authenticate strictly (via tokens) to access these services.
The external platform distributing the app. It is trusted to deliver non-tampered, signed binaries to the device.
